<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This is a follow-up fix for #25256.

#25256 added `torch.compile` to the Wan diffusion native layernorm paths to improve MUSA/CUDA inference speed. The compile decorator only disabled NPU:

```python
@torch.compile(disable=current_platform.is_npu())
```

However, on ROCm/HIP these diffusion layernorm custom ops use `forward_hip`, which intentionally falls back to `forward_native` because the CUDA/CuTeDSL fused kernels are not supported on HIP. After #25256, the HIP fallback path also went through `torch.compile`, which is not the supported ROCm path for these diffusion layernorm ops and caused the AMD diffusion tests to fail.

This PR disables `torch.compile` on HIP while keeping the #25256 behavior unchanged for the other platforms.

## Modifications

Disable `torch.compile` on ROCm/HIP for the three diffusion layernorm native fallback paths:

- `_ScaleResidualNormScaleShift.forward_native`
- `_NormScaleShift.forward_native`
- `_NormTanhMulAdd.forward_native`

The disable condition is changed from:

```python
current_platform.is_npu()
```

to:

```python
current_platform.is_npu() or current_platform.is_hip()
```

## Accuracy Tests

Test run: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26217994814

Passed AMD ROCm 7.2 diffusion server tests:

- `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd-rocm720`
- `multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu-amd-rocm720`

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed benchmark impact is expected on ROCm because this PR restores the native fallback behavior for HIP instead of enabling a new optimized path. The MUSA/CUDA `torch.compile` optimization from #25256 is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body: Thanks for this! Disabling the layernorm `torch.compile` path on ROCm landed on main via #29673, which covers all three `forward_native` paths, so I'm closing this as superseded. Feel free to reopen if something is still missing.

## Code Review

This pull request updates the `forward_native` methods in `layernorm.py` to disable `torch.compile` on HIP platforms, supplementing the existing NPU check. The reviewer recommends extending this disablement to MUSA and XPU platforms for consistency across all native fallback paths. Furthermore, the reviewer suggests using module-level variables like `_is_hip` instead of `current_platform.is_hip()` to improve code conciseness.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Since MUSA and XPU also fall back to `forward_native` (lines 486-494), it is recommended to disable `torch.compile` for them as well to ensure stability across all supported platforms. Additionally, using the module-level variables `_is_npu`, `_is_hip`, etc., would be more concise and consistent with the rest of the file.

```suggestion
    @torch.compile(disable=_is_npu or _is_hip or _is_musa or _is_xpu)
```
